nodes.title: fix(framework): rate-limit the MCP endpoints with a sliding window

nodes.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Tie the exemption to a real handshake**

Any authenticated Store API caller can repeatedly POST a body whose method is `notifications/initialized`, even without an MCP session header, and return before both the p

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decode before filtering valid initialized notifications**

The raw substring pre-check rejects valid JSON encodings before examining their decoded method. For example, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/\u

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route oversized initialized notifications to the handshake bucket**

When a valid `notifications/initialized` payload exceeds 4 KiB—for example because it contains legal JSON whitespace or an extended `_meta` obj

After this change, the handshake completes, but the first real request still gets HTTP 429, so #18906 stays unresolved. `TimeBackoffLimiter::consume()` restarts `timer` on every accepted request and never lowers `attempts` (`TimeBackoffLimiter.php:68-77`), so once a key has passed 300 requests, `tools/list` right after `initialize` hits `elapsed 0 < 60` (`TimeBackoff.php:98-105`) and gets 429.

`RateLimiterFactory.php:93-98` already passes any other policy to Symfony, so the cause can be fixed in configuration:

~~~yaml
mcp_admin_api:
    enabled: true
    policy: 'sliding_window'
    limit: 300
    interval: '60 seconds'
~~~

I suggest switching both `mcp_admin_api` and `mcp_store_api` to `sliding_window` and dropping the special case here. That needs a `RELEASE_INFO-6.7.md` entry for operators and an update of the rate-limiting docs.

The class docblock tells the #18906 story (what `time_backoff` does, "would otherwise get HTTP 429 (see #18906)"), and `AGENTS.md:198` repeats it almost word for word. The constant docblock at `:34-39` restates the method docblock at `:97-101`. The constraint worth keeping in source is one sentence: the follow-up must not share a counter with `initialize`, because `time_backoff` accepts a single request after the wait. The history belongs in the PR and the commit. If F1 is fixed by changing the policy, all three go.

nodes.body: `McpServerController.php:176` compares against `CallToolRequest::getMethod()`. The SDK ships `Mcp\Schema\Notification\InitializedNotification::getMethod()`, which returns `'notifications/initialized'`, and `mcp/sdk` is a hard `require` (`composer.json`, `src/Core/composer.json`). A `const` cannot hold a method call, so the comparison at `:125` would use it inline.

nodes.body: A domain that cannot produce a context now takes the whole check down, not just its own sales channel. `SalesChannelDomainContextFactory::create()` throws from `BaseSalesChannelContextFactory` when, for example, the domain's currency is no longer assigned to the sales channel (`src/Core/System/SalesChannel/Context/BaseSalesChannelContextFactory.php:114-121`). The exception escapes `doRun()` and `SystemChecker::runChecks()` turns it into a single `Failed to run the check with ERROR` result (`src/Core/Framework/SystemCheck/SystemChecker.php:73-77`), so the remaining sales channels are never probed and their `extra` entries are lost. The status stays `FAILURE`, so this is about diagnosability, not grading. Could we catch it per domain and record it as that domain's failure, like `SalesChannelDomainUtil::handleRequest()` does for the request? The same applies to `ProductListingReadinessCheck.php:135

nodes.body: The comment describes earlier revisions of this PR rather than the code. "Filtering on `available` instead would … keep dropping closeout products after an admin turned the setting off" argues against a filter that is no longer here. The same happens in `SalesChannelDomainProvider.php:26` ("which `GROUP BY sales_channel.id` alone does not"). `SalesChannelDomainContextFactory.php:36` also has a 162-character line in the middle of the docblock, and both checks repeat the same paragraph about the lookup context, which the factory's own docblock already covers. I suggest keeping the first sentence here ("Mirrors ProductDetailRoute::addCloseoutFilter()"), dropping the references to removed code, and linking the checks to the factory instead of repeating it.
